Federal Parliament National Assembly 20th Session Verbatim Record Chaitra 23, 2082, Monday Meeting Number: 3 The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 12:17 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal. The National Assembly's meeting today (12:17 PM) Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, - The proceedings will begin. Names of honorable members have been received to speak during Zero Hour. Honorable members are allocated 1/1 minute each to speak during Zero Hour. - First, Honorable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya. Honorable Mr. Krishna Prasad (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson, the NEPSE has fallen to 2,676, down from 2,774 before the election. In this period, investors have lost approximately 3 kharba. After the government was formed, industries and businesses were enthusiastic with a new and strong outlook. However, the actions taken by the government against industries and businesses mean that the capital market will not be able to grow further, according to the Stock Brokers Association, which has observed a continuous high decline in NEPSE, creating a negative narrative. Right Honorable Chairperson, due to the current situation, the risk of investors withdrawing from the market has increased. Through you, Right Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the serious attention of the Nepal Government to this matter. Thank you. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ghanashyam Rizal. (12:19 PM) Honorable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:19 PM) - On the evening of Chaitra 18, a vehicle hit Thakar Bahadur, a permanent resident of Ward No. 4 of Shailung Rural Municipality, Dolakha, on the flyover in Gwarko, Lalitpur, causing him serious injury. He is currently receiving treatment in an unconscious state at the nearby B&B Hospital. Due to his poor financial condition, his family is unable to afford further treatment, and the vehicle and driver involved in the accident have not yet been apprehended. I urge the government to arrange for the injured person's treatment and save his life. Furthermore, due to the failure to apprehend the drivers and owners responsible for accident treatment costs, many Nepalis are losing their lives unnecessarily due to their poor financial condition. Through you, Right Honorable Chairperson, I draw the government's attention to the need for a separate government fund to arrange treatment for such injured individuals and protect the citizens' right to life. Thank you. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar. (12:20 PM) Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:20 PM) - There are over 1.7 million Nepali workers in Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Dubai, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman. Due to the war between Iran and America, these Nepali workers are living under immense mental stress, fear, and anxiety. Their families and relatives in Nepal are drowning in tears, worrying about what will happen today or tomorrow. Some Nepali workers who contacted me said, 'Our votes are counted, our money is also somewhat counted, but our pain is not understood, Balen government.' Therefore, through you, Right Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the serious attention of the Nepal Government and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to provide necessary psychosocial counseling, security, and emergency rescue to these workers and inform them about it. Thank you. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Manrupa Sharma. (12:21 PM) Honorable Ms. Manrupa Sharma (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:21 PM) - Discussions are ongoing regarding the new government. Alongside this, the general public is suffering from inflation. With the price increase of food grains, petroleum products, and cooking gas, laborers are in distress. This is affecting urban dwellers and families with limited budgets the most. The country's economy is also impacted. The government has not introduced any action plan to address these issues. I urge the government to bring forth an action plan soon that will benefit the general public and, through you, Right Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to this. Thank you. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala. (12:21 PM) Honorable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:21 PM) - Today, the increasing cybercrime on social media has made everyone serious. Thousands of teenage girls, including very young girls aged five, have become victims of rape. Similarly, upon opening their mobile phones, many young men issue threats like 'I will rape you, I will throw you in jail,' and some teenage girls have reached depression due to insults and abuse. I want to clearly urge the government to enact stringent laws to stop cyberattacks. Those who misuse cyber technology should be identified and punished as soon as possible. The digital security of all women should be ensured. A special investigation committee should be formed to provide justice to the victims. Thank you. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Renu Chand. (12:23 PM) Honorable Ms. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:23 PM) - Fuel prices have increased, and gas availability is difficult, which increases inflation and has already raised prices. In the past, when the previous government increased petrol prices, the current Prime Minister strongly protested through social media and alerted the state to its responsibilities. Now, he himself is leading the government. I expect that the Prime Minister is serious about this responsibility and the problem. The war between America, Iran, and Israel does not seem to be ending immediately. Our destroyed structures will not be rebuilt overnight. Therefore, I want to draw the government's attention to this matter through you, Mr. Speaker, and urge the government to provide immediate relief as the kitchen has become expensive. Thank you. (12:24 PM) Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:24 PM) - Due to international conflicts, the prices of diesel, petrol, and cooking gas have skyrocketed. This has directly impacted the kitchens of Nepali citizens. But the main question is, will we always be dependent on imports? Will the Nepali citizens be left to suffer the burden of inflation even with a two-thirds majority government? I make a clear demand to the government: Reduce the taxes on petroleum products and provide immediate relief. Make electricity cheaper to encourage electric stoves (induction) and electric vehicles. Strictly monitor gas and electricity leakage in Dailekh. Right Honorable Chairperson, petroleum exploration holds great potential to make Nepal self-reliant. This should be pursued with high priority and at a rapid pace. Also, the two-day weekly holiday for employees should be reviewed. The public can no longer tolerate inflation. Relief is needed, alternatives are needed, and accountability is needed from the government. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma. (12:24 PM) Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:26 PM) - It is not good for our government to close government and educational institutions for two days citing the Middle East conflict. Government, what is the number of students in Nepal who walk to school or travel by their own vehicles? Nepal is a mountainous and impoverished country, so most of our children walk to school. Only a few use public transport, and public transport is not being closed, so why are only students being closed, government? This could create a situation where employees and students are unemployed for three days, including half a day on Friday. Through you, Right Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the attention of the Nepal Government to withdraw this decision and reopen the institutions. Thank you. Lal Salaam. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari. (12:26 PM) Honorable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:26 PM) - It is being said that the impact of the ongoing war in the Middle East is also being felt in the lives of Nepalis. The rescue of Nepali citizens stranded in the Middle East should not be delayed. Currently, due to the high tax rate imposed on petroleum products, inflation is severely affecting people. The daily lives of the public are becoming difficult due to the rising prices of daily necessities like oil, gas, and food items, and unemployment. Through you, Honorable Chairperson, I demand from the government effective market monitoring, control of rising inflation, and arrangements for the smooth supply of raw materials needed for Nepali industries. Thank you. Greetings. Right Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Savitri Malla. (12:27 PM) Honorable Ms. Savitri Malla (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:27 PM) - Due to repeated excessive price hikes in fuel and gas by the Nepal Oil Corporation, citing national and international reasons, transportation and freight charges have increased, leading to a significant price rise in daily construction materials. Furthermore, a shortage of daily necessities has emerged. As a result, general consumers, the public, and citizens are forced to endure inflation and scarcity. Therefore, through you, Mr. Speaker, I want to draw the government's attention to immediately adjust the excessive price hikes in fuel and gas, control price increases, and take immediate steps to make daily necessities available. Also, I want to draw the government's attention through this assembly to prioritize the current stage of petroleum and gas exploration in Dailekh in the current budget and policy program. Thank you. Greetings. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the Zero Hour session concludes with the speeches of the Honorable Members. (12:28 PM) I will provide time to the remaining newly elected Honorable Members in order. I have allocated 4/5 minutes to each Honorable Member to speak. First, Honorable Member Jagat Timilsina. Honorable Mr. Jagat Timilsina (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson, (12:29 PM) - How the country is run, what the condition of the country is, Honorable Members, Jai Nepal. The way universities are run and their condition serve as a mirror to this. Therefore, higher education is the backbone of any country today, and I believe the National Assembly should play an important role in ensuring quality education at all levels in Nepal by actively playing a role in education policy and budget management for the improvement of higher education quality. Similarly, the National Assembly should play an important role in promoting higher education and research, and I want to state in this esteemed assembly that scientific research, innovation, and knowledge production should be prioritized nationally by coordinating with universities and research centers. The effective functioning of the National Assembly committees will have a significant contribution from the members of this National Assembly, and I also want to state here that the regular evaluation of the committees' performance should ensure transparency and impartiality. Similarly, to play an effective role in strengthening federalism...

We must all contribute to initiating laws and policies to provide genuine assistance, resources, and authority to local governments. I also state here that the National Assembly should play a significant role in advancing corruption control as a national agenda. I wish to state before you all that I will increase corruption monitoring in all public bodies and implement effective oversight and accountability processes. Similarly, I wish to state that the National Assembly should play a significant role in establishing good governance and making the role of the National Assembly effective, and that transparency and inclusivity should be ensured in the implementation of government policies, budgets, and plans. I also wish to state that the National Assembly should play a significant role in citizen participation and transparency. To this end, the National Assembly should take initiative to make citizen suggestions, public hearings, and reporting systems in government bodies effective, raise the problems and difficulties of local levels in the National Assembly, and I have also stated here that we, the honorable members of the National Assembly, must put pressure on the government to pay attention to such issues and solve the problems. Raising these issues in the National Assembly, I express my gratitude to the Nepali Congress for nominating me as a candidate for the National Assembly, and I bid farewell, thanking the members of the Provincial Assembly, the Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Chairpersons, and Vice-Chairpersons of Gandaki Province who gave me their votes in the National Assembly election on Magh 29th, leading to my victory. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
(12:33 PM)
Honorable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(12:34 PM)
Distinguished members of the National Assembly, today is my first day. On my behalf, I offer heartfelt tributes to the unknown brave martyrs. I am grateful for the opportunity to speak and present myself in the House today. I express my gratitude to the policymakers and constitution makers. I am able to speak because of them. My political guru, who brought me this far, is Sheikh Idris, and I offer him heartfelt tributes. I want to share a small anecdote about him. There are two or three honorable members here who spent time with him. His principle was "to accommodate everyone, to include everyone, to seat everyone." I am deeply touched by this. A small incident from one day: our old friends, including Dungiraj Shastri, Jagannath Acharya, and Kapledhar Kayastha, came. He always used to sit on the floor. After they came, he had a habit of eating paan, he used to eat paan. And he would break a single paan into small pieces and share it with everyone, sitting with them and feeding them. Especially, the principle of accommodating everyone that I learned from him, I want to express my deep gratitude to the party that has brought me this far. First and foremost, I want to thank the Chief Minister of Madhesh Province, the ministers, mayors, deputy mayors, chairpersons, vice-chairpersons, and all my colleagues who gave me their votes in the election and brought me here. Thank you.
Now, regarding the government, the apology the government has made to our Dalit community is a good and commendable thing. However, such incidents have happened before. It happened in South Africa and Germany. Along with the apology, there was also deceit later. To ensure that such things do not happen in the future, I thank them on behalf of the entire Dalit community. He has done a very good job. In the way that the Madhesi Dalits are very backward, he has made a member from the "Vadi" community a minister. I thank him very much. Because this is a commendable act. Furthermore, he has spoken about good governance. The first step, the first stride, the first point of good governance is representation. The fact that not a single representative from our Madhesh community has come to the House of Representatives is, in my opinion and in the opinion of our community, not a good sign. Now, I am speaking here today on behalf of 17.29 percent Dalits. And for them, I will support them in the National Assembly on many occasions regarding their issues and concerns. Thank you.
(12:39 PM)
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal.
(12:39 PM)
Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dangal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I want to offer heartfelt tributes to all the brave martyrs who have attained martyrdom. I want to congratulate and extend best wishes for a successful term to all the honorable members of Bagmati Province, the newly elected members of the village municipalities, and all the newly elected honorable members. I also want to express my gratitude for the role played by my party, the CPN UML, in nominating me as a candidate for the National Assembly from Bagmati Province and ensuring my victory. Studying the National Assembly, I see that we have experts, intellectuals, and highly experienced individuals from the political field, as well as leaders from various sectors, honorable members. We also have honorable members who have gained recognition through social mobilization. All of this is a dynamic that we have among us, and from this dynamic, we can achieve very significant accomplishments. I believe this is especially true in the field of legislation. To make this National Assembly more effective and enhance its dignity, I, and my party, pledge to play a positive and effective role. Specifically, regarding lawmaking and the creation of acts, I have studied three stages. The first stage is the pre-legislative stage of lawmaking. This begins from the ministry, receives theoretical approval from the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal, and then involves certain procedures. The state, especially the government, has a very important role in this, and the role of the honorable members in this space seems a bit weak to me. Therefore, our initiative needs to be directed more towards that. In other words, our participation must be ensured in the very first stage of legislative drafting. I would like to draw the attention of the honorable members to what needs to be done for this. The second stage is the stage of drafting the bill and making it an act. In this, we engage in intensive discussions, interactions, consultations, debates, and so forth, and we will enrich it. That is our commitment. And the tasks we need to perform after post-legislation is enacted. This includes monitoring, submitting reports to the Government of Nepal regarding its implementation, and playing a role in its effective implementation. I think we need to show more interest and pay more attention to this. Therefore, I am not going to elaborate on many issues here. We have a great asset among us. That asset is that our country is multi-ethnic, multilingual, multi-religious, multicultural, and geographically diverse, and with this geographical diversity, we must unite our country within this dynamic. We must seek unity within diversity. We must increase the tolerance of Nepali society, increase goodwill, end all forms of discrimination, whether class, caste, regional, gender, linguistic, religious, and all forms of exploitation, oppression, discrimination, untouchability, and move forward. Not only this, but based on the principle of participatory development with proportional inclusive representation, what we have envisioned is an egalitarian society. We have a great task, a great responsibility among us, in our work. Therefore, there are many aspects to building this egalitarian society. This includes the issue of equal rights, the issue of ending discrimination, the issues of effective participation in policy-making with meaningful presence of stakeholders, and the issues of social justice. We need to accomplish all these tasks. Therefore, the constitution has guided us in this direction. Finally, I would like to state that our party's respected Chairman and former Prime Minister, respected Comrade KP Oli, is currently in custody. His unjust and vindictive arrest should be immediately revoked. Justice should be done to him. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhal.
(12:45 PM)
Honorable Mr. Meena Singh Rakhal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I thank you for the time and I thank the members of the Provincial Assembly and local heads and deputy heads who elected and sent me here. Through this respected House, I want to express my commitment to the country and the people. I offer tributes to the martyrs and wish the injured a speedy recovery. I congratulate the Honorable Prime Minister and the ministers.
I will always remain steadfast in promoting the main tenet of democracy in the protection of the constitution and adherence to the law. I will raise the voices of the people strongly in the House and will continuously strive to solve their problems, and it will be my duty. Zero tolerance against corruption will not be compromised in establishing good governance. I will work above personal interests for the nation's prosperity, development, and stability, and I pledge to do so. I promise to remain honest in my responsibilities and continuously dedicated to the welfare of the nation and its people.
Honorable Chairperson, Karnali Province is rich in natural resources, yet it is still the most backward in basic development indicators. The poverty rate in Karnali is around 30 percent, which is much higher than the national average. Per capita income is also the lowest in the country. The situation in the health sector is even more serious. Many districts lack specialist doctors, and patients are forced to be carried on stretchers for hours. The literacy rate is only about 65 percent. Honorable Chairperson, students are forced to go abroad for higher education. Regarding infrastructure, many settlements are still far from road access. During the rainy season, transportation is disrupted for months. This is not just a statistic; it is the daily suffering of the citizens of Karnali. Young people are forced to go abroad in search of employment. Mothers and fathers cry with pain when they send their children far away. Therefore, I strongly demand that Karnali be declared a special priority area and a policy be brought to link local resources and means with employment.
Chairperson, I wish to raise a very serious issue in this respected House. The treatment meted out to our party's respected Chairman and former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and the leader of the Nepali Congress and former Home Minister is not a minor incident. Honorable Speaker, this is not just an action against one person. It is a direct attack on democracy, the constitution, and the rule of law. Chairperson, today an injustice is done to one leader, but tomorrow injustice can reach every citizen. We have clearly seen that political actions are taken above legal processes.

Retaliatory games are being played. This is a very dangerous symptom for democracy. The work of suppressing voices that weaken democracy and targeting the opposition should be stopped immediately. I demand from the honorable house that KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak be released immediately. Ensure fair and transparent legal process. End political revenge. Otherwise, this will not be limited to voices within the house. The voice of the people will roar from the streets, and the government will be entirely responsible for it. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ranjit Karna. (12:49 PM) Honorable Mr. Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, I offer my heartfelt tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for democracy and human rights, standing in this esteemed assembly. I am honored to have the opportunity to speak at this rostrum for the first time as a member of the National Assembly. This parliament is not just a place for speeches; it is a national responsibility with the mandate to transform people's expectations into national policy. I will always be committed to maintaining the dignity of the parliament and fostering public trust. Chairperson, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the government led by the National Independent Party, formed through the recently concluded elections, on behalf of myself and my party, the Nepali Congress. This mandate is the people's aspiration for change, and such public practice is the erosion of democracy. In a democracy, the people's mandate is supreme. The history of the Nepali Congress is intertwined with every political change in Nepal. It is because of the democratic foundation built by the people's movements from 2007 BS to 2062/63 BS that the new generation has the opportunity to flourish today. This is a testament to our political openness and institutional maturity. However, Chairperson, along with our glorious past, we must also acknowledge our weaknesses. Although constitution and rights have been ensured, good governance, employment, and prosperity have not reached the people as expected. Delays, policy obstacles, and weaknesses in controlling corruption have been observed. Youth unemployment has made foreign employment a compulsion. The reality today is that we have been unable to ensure quality services in basic sectors like education and health as per public expectations, and we have not been able to move forward with a clear roadmap for good governance, transparency, employment, and social justice. This must be rectified now. The Congress has experience, energy, and innovative thinking, while the government also has energy and a desire for innovation. The combination of these two can give the country the right momentum. There is significant similarity between the vision of our party president, the respected Gagan Kumar Thapa, and the Nepali Congress's Vision Ten, and the government's agenda. We are ready to cooperate in controlling corruption, strengthening institutions, and administrative reform. We will fully support positive proposals. The Nepali Congress (transformed Congress, with the vision of a changed nation) is focused on youth self-employment, innovation, and utilizing the skills of migrants. We will remain supportive of the government in creating opportunities within the country. Learning from our achievements in international relations and past weaknesses, and considering the changing global environment, how can Nepal's national interest be protected? For that, the Congress will always stand with the government in its efforts to take concrete steps towards rapid economic development through prudent diplomatic practice and effective economic diplomacy. We will also be positive and liberal towards the government's initiatives to facilitate the private sector, boost morale, accelerate economic activities, and establish good governance through transparent regulatory processes. Chairperson, our constitution is a historic document in world history. We are ready to make it more people-friendly through amendments to keep the constitution alive. By prioritizing national interest above political prejudice on development agendas, the Congress is ready to play the role of not just a 'constructive opposition' but a responsible partner. I firmly believe that we will stand with every step taken in the interest of the country and democracy. If there is any anti-people decision made by violating laws and procedures against democracy and public interest, we will protest and resist it. I want to make it clear to the government. Finally, I urge the honorable Prime Minister: come, let us build national unity, let us cooperate to prepare agendas. Our views may differ until the election, our parties may be different, but after the election, our goal is the same: a prosperous Nepal, dignified Nepalis. The Nepali Congress, being a party that fights for the change of an era, wants to move forward hand in hand with the new generation. For this, we do not want to be an obstacle; we want to engage in meaningful dialogue. Parliament is the common ground for that dialogue. If the parliament weakens, democracy also weakens. Thank you. Jai Nepal. (12:54 PM) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri. Honorable Mr. Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I feel extremely proud to be present in this esteemed hall of the National Assembly. This is also an opportunity to be inspired by the good and diverse practices in the National Assembly. For this, I express my gratitude, and at the same time, I remember my party, which elected me to this National Assembly, the coalition parties associated with this party, and all the respected members of the Provincial Assembly of Lumbini Province, the chiefs and deputy chiefs of local levels of Lumbini Province, and all the voters. We have some good practices. Through those practices, the role I play in the National Assembly is for the entire country, especially for Lumbini Province, and for the responsibilities and duties that our voters in Lumbini Province gave us during the election. I will always pledge to remember those responsibilities. I want to take many things from this National Assembly as memories. Especially in the context of working with new concepts, we will do that. In this context, the democratic system we are practicing today. I also express my heartfelt respect to all the martyrs who sacrificed their lives during this change and throughout this transformation. Along with respecting the martyrs, today's society and what we have achieved in this society, and from what state we have come here today. There are many unanswered questions regarding this. I feel that these questions should be left in the National Assembly. I cannot guarantee when the answers, investigations, prosecutions, and reports of these will be resolved in history. But some questions must be left behind. In that context, we, especially the political parties involved in all the revolutions of 2062/63 BS, 2046 BS, and 2007 BS, are saying today that everything is fine. There is a need to re-evaluate whether all this was fine or not. Saying all this was fine is not true. But saying all was bad is also not true. To bring society to this point, we had good practices in different periods. From those practices, we have achieved today's refined society. In this too, we have faced many ups and downs in the journey of its social structures. We have faced many difficulties in accepting the coexistence of society. We also sought to create a kind of existential society today. Today's change is not just any change. This change is an achievement resulting from a very big concept, a great contribution, a great sacrifice. But while achieving all this, why couldn't we preserve all these things in society as they were? Why are our young people unhappy with this structure, this system, and all these things? Today, I feel that there were some things wrong. We did not provide opportunities to correct those mistakes. Therefore, in any democratic society, citizens have the right to revolt against any power peacefully. But was the rebellion of Bhadra 23 and 24 peaceful? Or was it a violent rebellion? Who will take responsibility for it? Some reports came about the incident of the 23rd. On the 24th, these destroyed Singha Durbar, these burnt things, and the narrative that nothing will happen by burning the state against the state, and who sent people to monitor it like that. Who will find the answer to this? Who created the narrative that it is okay to burn Singha Durbar today, that nothing will happen by burning it, and who used the youth in this way? The answer to this will be sought not today, but tomorrow, and someday by this honorable National Assembly. I believe that our successors will also seek it. I don't think it's right to sweep the dust under the carpet and say everything is fine. Based on the premise that the incident of Bhadra 23 was peaceful, today Singha Durbar has become ruins. In a way, I am not a witness to the ruins of this Singha Durbar. At one time, I was also a leader in its reconstruction. Therefore, more than anyone else, I am concerned about what happened in history. When will its impartial investigation take place? At what level will the state take responsibility for this? I want to leave these questions here. I will also try to find the answers to these questions throughout my tenure. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha. (1:00 PM) Honorable Ms. Rekha Kumari Jha (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I feel honored to be present in the National Assembly. Similarly, according to last year's data, there are records of 260 incidents of violence against women in Madhesh Province, with the highest number of incidents recorded in Dhanusha district. According to the data, 62.3 percent are domestic violence. The highest percentage, 9.96 percent, are from family members within the home, revealing the reality of higher risk within the home. The age group of 18 to 35 years appears to be the most affected. Similarly, reasons include dowry shortage, family pressure to marry, preference for having daughters, beauty prejudices, and other traditional customs. The data also shows that in Madhesh, it is still a practice for women to obtain citizenship only after marriage. It has been found that women affected by violence are deprived of the right to citizenship, their marriages are not registered, and their dependent children are deprived of birth registration, nutritious food, and other essential services. If the rate of domestic violence in Madhesh is to be reduced, it is necessary for the government to provide age-appropriate skill training to everyone in every household. It is also necessary to encourage them to pursue professions according to their skills. Honorable Chairperson, it is necessary to be prepared to enact and continue the Civil Service Act. Today, employees have been working for the 10th year, but their promotions have not been seen. Honorable Chairperson, it is seen that only those who have connections get promoted. Honorable Chairperson, if the state proceeds in an illegal, unconstitutional, prejudiced, and retaliatory manner, it raises serious questions about democracy itself. This violates the effectiveness of law and governance, political freedom, and human rights. Therefore, I strongly demand the immediate release of former Prime Minister Mr. KP Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Mr. Ramesh Lekhak. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe.

(1:03 PM) Honorable Ms. Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected Chairperson
(1:04 PM) Sir, today I stand to address this esteemed National Assembly meeting for the first time, feeling joy, pride, and a deep sense of responsibility. On this occasion, I express my heartfelt tribute to all known and unknown martyrs who sacrificed their precious lives for democracy, republic, and federalism, and I wish to express my highest respect for their sacrifice. Respected Chairperson, remembering the dignity of this National Assembly, its institutional existence, and its role as a forum for intellectual and inclusive discourse, I express my heartfelt gratitude to our party's esteemed chairperson and former Prime Minister, Honorable KP Sharma Oli, as well as the party leadership, for providing the historic opportunity for a woman from the minority Mechhe community to reach such a dignified house. I also thank the respected provincial assembly members of Koshi Province, the people's representatives, and all supporters who voted for me with trust and made me victorious. I wish the current elected government heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to work by embracing the rule of law and constitutional supremacy in the interest of the people and the nation. There will always be constructive support and cooperation for the positive, public-interest-oriented, and nation-benefiting work done by the government. I will also continuously raise my voice to ensure accountability for actions that adversely affect the nation and public interest. Respected Chairperson, speaking of oversight, I express regret over the step taken within 24 hours of the government's formation, which challenged the rule of law with a vindictive spirit against former Prime Minister and party chairman Honorable KP Sharma Oli. Similarly, such decisions based on the recommendations of a controversial commission whose legality is questionable have raised serious questions about the rule of law and constitutional dignity. Furthermore, I wish to draw the government's serious attention to the increasing cyberbullying, arrests, and creation of a fearful environment against women and citizens, which is being observed based on the issues raised by the government. Respected Chairperson, the National Assembly has historically played an important role as a forum for legislation, policy guidance, and inclusive debate. It has strengthened democracy by providing deep discourse, balance, and stability in policy-making. Therefore, we need to move towards solutions, not just by identifying problems. I believe in a solution-oriented and results-focused work style. My firm commitment is to advance policy debates based on facts, evidence, and logic, keeping the issues of marginalized communities and women at the center, embracing the Sustainable Development Goals. Respected Chairperson, Nepal's sovereignty, independence, and national integrity are the basis of our existence and future. National independence and citizens' rights have an inseparable and deep relationship. Until all citizens receive a dignified life, equal opportunities, and access to justice, our sovereignty cannot be fully strengthened. Due to a lack of inclusivity in policy-making, delays in the development process, weaknesses in implementation, and a lack of good governance, public trust appears to be weakening. Only when our education undergoes qualitative change, and health services and employment become reliable for everyone, will trust in the state grow stronger. We make laws, policies, and regulations, but due to a lack of effective implementation, the gap between policy and practice remains. Amidst these challenges, I wish to present myself as a responsible bridge to reduce the gap between policy and implementation, and to strengthen coordination between federal, provincial, and local levels. Moving forward by incorporating past experiences and the energy of youth is the need of the hour. I believe that we can move towards real change only when every policy has a clear action plan, timeline, and accountability. In conclusion, a nation becomes strong when governance is based not only on power but also on accountability and the trust of its citizens. Through this esteemed house, I heartily appeal to all honorable members to keep the national interest at the center through cooperation, unity, and positive competition... time is up.)
Respected Chairperson:- Honorable Member Lalit Jang Shahi.
(1:09 PM) Honorable Mr. Lalit Jang Shahi (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson,
(1:10 PM) Sir, as I stand at this rostrum to speak, I wish to express my highest respect and heartfelt tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their precious lives for the people and democracy of this country at various times since 2007. I also wish to express my heartfelt gratitude and thanks to my party, the Nepali Congress, and its esteemed leaders for providing me the opportunity to reach here from Karnali Province's other group as a member of the National Assembly, and to the honorable members of the Provincial Assembly of Karnali Province, the mayors and deputy mayors, the chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of rural municipalities, and the respected voters who cast their valuable votes for me when I was a candidate. As a member of the National Assembly, I pledge to raise my voice to keep the dignity and image of the National Assembly high and clean, and to make its role effective.
Respected Chairperson, our country Nepal falls among two and a half dozen countries in the world. It seems to me that we need to seriously consider why the narrative that "the system changed but the situation did not" has been created even after reaching the 21st century. Rising above personal and party interests, and with consensus, cooperation, and unity, we must first ensure that nationality is not weakened, democracy is not weakened, and while amendments and revisions to the constitution of 2072, which our Nepali people achieved through seven decades of struggle, may happen in a manner appropriate to the times, I believe we must also be serious about protecting this constitution. The narrative that nothing happened after 2046/047 is not something I agree with. Much has happened, but not everything. Now, with a government formed with political majority, along with control of corruption, good governance, and transparency, stability must be established. Currently, with a nearly two-thirds majority, we are relieved that political instability and the lack of a stable government will not occur for at least the next 4 years. May a new era of good governance and development begin. May the spirit of patriotism awaken in everyone. I conclude my remarks with the commitment that all of us Nepalis will now unite to build the nation.
Thank you.
Jai Nepal.
Respected Chairperson: - Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari.
(1:14 PM) Honorable Ms. Lila Kumari Bhandari (Nepal Communist Party, UML):-
(1:14 PM) Respected Chairperson, I sincerely thank the respected Chairperson of this assembly for inviting me to present my views on this important occasion of the commencement of the 20th session of the National Assembly. My party's decision to elect me to the National Assembly is paramount, and I sincerely thank our party's respected leader, the party chairman KP Sharma Oli, and the party's top leaders. On this occasion, I sincerely thank the people of Sudurpashchim who gave me their valuable votes to make me victorious, and through the rostrum of this assembly, I express my thanks to the respected Chairperson, the Vice-Chairpersons of the municipalities, and all.
Respected Chairperson, I pay my heartfelt tribute and express my respect to all the great martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the repeated movements that brought the country to its current situation. And I sincerely thank all the political parties that have fulfilled their roles as the country has reached this point after overcoming many ups and downs in the history of movements.
Respected Chairperson, a government led by the Rastriya Swatantra Party was formed on Chaitra 13, 2082 BS. I wish the Honorable Prime Minister of the Government of Nepal, Balen Shah, and all the members of his cabinet a successful tenure, and I wish them success in the future in building a plan for the country's accountability and responsibility. I urge the government to consider the direct impact on our country due to the ongoing war in the Middle Eastern countries, which has led to daily price hikes and black marketing, making the public distressed. In this challenging time, everyone must be responsible, but the Government of Nepal, which plays the role of guardian of the people, must be even more responsible and accountable. Through the Chairperson, I wish to draw the government's attention to this.
In the recent period, we must think about where this increasing digital violence, rape, and other heinous crimes against our women sisters are taking Nepali society. I urge the Government of Nepal to immediately enact effective laws to end this dire situation and to be serious about justice for those sisters who have fallen victim to crime and have been forced to die, and who are suffering from depression. I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal through the Honorable Minister, who is also present.
Respected Chairperson, the newly formed government has taken the oath of office. We all have the self-realization that the government has become somewhat irresponsible and has proceeded illegally. All three tiers of the country must remain within their respective boundaries and defined responsibilities, and we have felt since the formation of the government that it is overstepping its boundaries. The government's vindictive, prejudiced, and illegal behavior towards political leadership in the recent period must end. My suggestion to the government, which has resorted to vindictive behavior and illegal arrests, is that the country can never move forward or function with revenge. Therefore, the Government of Nepal should function legally, rising above revenge politics and prejudiced politics. We are all law-abiding citizens. None of us are above the law. Therefore, I demand the immediate release of Honorable leader KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak, who have been arrested unconstitutionally, illegally, prejudicially, and vindictively.
Similarly, Respected Chairperson, due to the war in the Middle East, millions of Nepalis working in foreign employment are living a life of tragedy. The government, with a nearly two-thirds majority, has the role of guardian for all Nepalis who have gone abroad for employment and are living in fear of war. It is a strong government. Thank you.
Respected Chairperson: - Honorable Member Basudev Ghimire.
(1:20 PM) Honorable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson,
(1:20 PM) Honorable members, I feel honored to stand and speak in this esteemed assembly for the first time in my life. At this moment, I first pay tribute to all the immortal martyrs who attained martyrdom in the revolutions and various people's movements and struggles from 2007 until today, and I express my highest respect to the injured and the families of the martyrs. I express my gratitude to the central leadership of the Nepali Congress for the contribution made by my party, the Nepali Congress, by giving me the ticket for the National Assembly.

I express my gratitude and thank the honorable members of Lumbini Province who elected me, the chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of municipalities and rural municipalities from all twelve districts of Lumbini Province, and the mayors and deputy mayors of municipalities. I would like to congratulate the members of the National Assembly elected in the election held on January 11th and the members of the House of Representatives elected in the election held on March 7th.
Today, the country is in a crisis, and I wish success and a fruitful tenure to the government led by Balen Shah, the independent party which has reached close to a two-thirds majority.
The country is currently in a crisis. When BP Koirala came to Nepal in 1976, the Asian continent was shrouded in dark clouds, and the country is in precisely that situation today. In this situation, if the party in power and the current government do not pursue national unity and reconciliation but instead advance with arrogance, revenge, and greed, driven by whims and impulses, and swayed by emotions, this course of action will not benefit the country. In this state where the nation's sovereignty is extremely weakened, as Girija Babu said, there is an extreme need for national consensus, cooperation, and unity. The public has realized this. Today, the public has voted for this government with hope, faith, and trust. In the past, we did many things. Some tasks remained unfinished, but we failed to understand the people. We couldn't win their emotions. We won their hearts, but not their votes. That may be the case. However, if the government does not proceed on the basis of cooperation, consensus, and national unity in this situation, the country will weaken, and the nation's sovereignty will weaken. In this situation, may this government work with the strength of consensus, cooperation, and unity. Wishing it well, I would like to conclude my remarks by suggesting that the government understand that the nation is the sentiment of the people, not just land and soil. With this suggestion and advice to the government through the honorable chairperson, I wish for the government to move forward on the basis of cooperation, consensus, and unity. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota.
(13:24 hrs)
Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson of the National Assembly, I express my heartfelt gratitude to this glorious house for allowing me to speak. I pay homage to all the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the state. We are practicing democracy today on the foundation of their sacrifices. I pay my respects to them. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the newly elected member of the House of Representatives and the new government led by the honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah for a successful tenure. Today, standing in this glorious assembly, I express my heartfelt gratitude to my family, my village Narethar, the people of my district Gorkha, and the representatives and general public of Gandaki Province for their support and inspiration throughout my political journey. I also extend my congratulations and best wishes to the newly elected honorable members of the National Assembly. Honorable Chairperson, this house is not just a place for speeches but also an institution for lawmaking and guiding the nation's long-term direction. The extraordinary mandate received by the current government is rare in democratic parliamentary practice. I wish the new government success in working with a long-term national interest in mind rather than momentary impulses. Our support will be in this.
Honorable Chairperson, even as we approach the end of the 21st century, incidents of domestic and sexual violence and social discrimination continue to occur, making it imperative to preserve social and moral values and awareness. In my nearly four-decade-long social and political journey, I have had the opportunity to closely observe both sides of gender-based violence. We must be prepared to amend laws to provide justice based on victimhood, perpetrator, and oppression, rather than gender. It is necessary to enact legal provisions to control cyberbullying and social offenses through the misuse of social media and bring the culprits to justice. Today, thousands of young women are being raped every moment. The government must take responsibility for this.
Honorable Chairperson, today I also wish to express my commitment to some issues from my district. My district, Gorkha, is not just the name of a district; it is the basis of Nepal's existence and identity. We must respect Gorkha's historical significance and connect it with national development. I request through this house that policies be amended to make Gorkha's headquarters the center and gateway for visiting historical and tourist destinations such as Manaslu and Chum Valley, the earthquake epicenter Barpak, Narad Pokhari, Dudh Pokhari, Nage Pokhari, Gorakhkali, and Manakamana. I appeal to develop Gorkha district as a living historical museum, connecting Gorkha's pride and historical heritage with tourism to further support Gorkha's trade and business. The Budhi Gandaki Hydropower Project, Gorakhkali Rubber Industry, and Pushpalal Mid-Hill Highway are national pride projects falling under the jurisdiction of the federal government. I request and inform that the federal government should make plans to expedite and complete these. Our nation, Nepal, is a unique country rich in natural, religious, and spiritual diversity, a rare and unparalleled gift to the world. This must be systematically linked with the nation's economic and cultural development, and I request the Government of Nepal to formulate and advance policies for the conservation and utilization of Nepal's water, land, and herbs, as well as tourism promotion and its comprehensive action plan.
Respected Chairperson, I demand the immediate release of our leader KP Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak, who have been illegally detained, and I earnestly request their release through this house. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa.
(13:30 hrs)
Honorable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, I am happy to stand before you today, having come from the Constituent Assembly, the second House of Representatives, to the National Assembly. Secondly, I thank my party, the Nepali Congress, for nominating me and allowing me to represent Koshi Province. First and foremost, after the Balen government has come into power, discussions about constitutional amendments have arisen. The Nepali Congress party is open to constitutional amendments. However, it should not be forgotten that we could not bring the constitution in the first Constituent Assembly. We brought this constitution with great difficulty in the second meeting of the Constituent Assembly, with the participation of 32 parties and two independent members. Some of our colleagues who were involved in the writing of that constitution are also among us here in the National Assembly. Therefore, I say that the Government of Nepal must bring this constitution by incorporating the wishes of all indigenous peoples, ethnic groups, youth, Madhesi, and Dalits, and by bringing this constitution together.
We must not forget that Nepal's every movement, whether it was in 2007 BS, 2017 BS, 2036 BS, or the recent youth movement, has led to elections in 2082 BS. Not only that, but I believe that the families of those who played a role and were martyred in bringing the federal democratic republic constitution to Nepal since 2007 BS should be honored and treated equally. Because today I hear that only the martyrs of the youth movement are being honored, therefore, I believe that we should honor and treat equally all those who have been involved since the Constituent Assembly since 2007 BS. Look. The narrative here is that the members of the National Assembly will obstruct various upcoming laws, acts, and bills. I want to clarify that we will not go down that path. We have come with a sense of responsibility. We have taken responsibility. We know our responsibility. We are here to build the nation and provide good governance. I also want to inform the Government of Nepal that we will play a complementary role in the good bills that you bring for nation-building. We will not be obstacles because we are also responsible.
Secondly, today, we are not deprived of the right to information, the right to information granted by the Constitution of Nepal. Because the report of the Karki Commission, which originated from the youth movement, has not yet been made public, but some individuals have been prosecuted based on that commission's report. We want to know the reasons for the prosecution, and at the same time, we request that the report of the National Human Rights Commission be presented as soon as possible because when the Government of Nepal goes to the United Nations High Commissioner's meeting in the near future, those reports will be sought. Therefore, I assert that Nepalis should receive their right to information. Today, Nepal's path is blocked in the economic sector, and I believe this government must bring new rules and laws to advance the economic sector because the country prospers through economic development. Secondly, today, the fight against inflation in the mid-hills has led to soaring prices in Nepal. I would like to remind you that I believe it is possible to facilitate this with petrol from the petroleum pipeline brought a long time ago. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel.
(13:35 hrs)
Honorable Member Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, I express my heartfelt gratitude to the honorable chairperson for the opportunity to speak at the podium of this esteemed National Assembly. On this occasion, I pay tribute to all the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the country's independence, people's rights, and livelihood. I express high respect to all the elders. I express my heartfelt gratitude to my party, CPN UML, for nominating me as a candidate to represent this house from Koshi Province, to the party leadership, to all the leaders of the Nepali Congress who supported it, to all the 93 members of the Provincial Assembly of Koshi Province who elected me, and to the chairpersons, vice-chairpersons, mayors, and deputy mayors of all 137 local levels. As representatives, we are naturally accountable to the people. Simultaneously, as representatives elected from the Provincial Assembly and local levels, we are even more accountable to the Provincial Assembly and local levels. I express my commitment to fulfilling that accountability. At the same time, as a representative of the oppressed Dalit community, which has faced oppression since historical times, I want to express that my voice in this house will be the common voice of those communities.
Honorable Chairperson, a government with a two-thirds majority has been formed after an immense public mandate.

6. Balen Shah "Walendra Shah" has been appointed as the Prime Minister. I wish him a successful tenure in the current government formed under his leadership. I congratulate all of them. Honorable Chairperson, during the elections, the Rastriya Swatantra Party put forward the slogan of good governance. The public trusted it and gave it a two-thirds majority. Today, we have the Good Governance Act as existing law. That act states that the rule of law is recognized as an important standard for good governance. Today, citing the commission formed to investigate the movement of Bhadra 23 and 24, and citing the commission's report, former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak have been arrested. It is reported that the Council of Ministers made a decision and the Ministry of Home Affairs issued an order for their detention. Which investigative body has been assigned? I urge that our law... Through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to ask the government: Does our law empower the Home Minister to approve? Through the Honorable Chairperson, I urge the government. We are currently in a democratic system. We currently adhere to constitutional supremacy. We are in a system of constitutional supremacy. However, the government is placing legislation in the supremacy of the Council of Ministers, and I urge a return to the rule of law through the Honorable Chairperson. Honorable Chairperson, our constitution states that all sovereign powers of the country shall be vested in the Council of Ministers. Similarly, Article 162 of the constitution states that executive powers within the province shall reside in the Provincial Council of Ministers, subject to the constitution and provincial laws. Likewise, executive powers at the local level shall reside in the rural and municipal executive bodies in accordance with the constitution and federal laws. A circular was issued by the Prime Minister's Office on Chaitra 18. A circular has been issued up to the local level regarding who to give advertisements to and who not to. Has this curtailed the rights of those bodies? I ask the government. Will our local governments, our provincial governments, operate according to the constitution and laws, or will they have to operate based on a circular from a federal ministry? I heartily urge a return to the rule of law through the Honorable Chairperson. Finally, I want to express my commitment to always protect the supremacy of the constitution, the rule of law, and the rights of the people in this House, and I commit to not letting the white Dhaka topi and shawl I am wearing be stained in any way. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mahanta Thakur. Called a little later (1:41 PM). He did not come, thinking he would be late. Honorable members, I inform you that the turn of the newly elected honorable members to speak has ended. Honorable members, now, in accordance with Rule (8) of the National Assembly Regulations, 2075, the process related to the election of the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly will commence. In accordance with the election program for the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, a proposal has been received that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker. Honorable members, I now grant permission to the proposer of the said proposal, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal, to present the proposal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Time: 10 minutes. Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I stand to present the proposal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected as the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Before presenting the proposal, I seek permission to share a few things about Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari. Honorable Chairperson, Lila Kumari Bhandari was actively involved in the country's democratic movement during her student days, right from the beginning of her student life. We are informed that she was subjected to various forms of repression while raising the common problems of students. In this context, in 2054 BS, she became involved as a member of the then CPN (Maoist) and participated in the armed conflict. As she continued to take on responsibilities, she also assumed the responsibility of a central committee member of that party and fulfilled it competently. Following the peace process, especially after the second People's Movement of 2062/063 BS, she became a candidate in the first Constituent Assembly election and was victorious. She played a very competent role in the first Constituent Assembly. In the course of taking on other responsibilities of the state, she also had the opportunity to serve as the State Minister for Education. In the context of assuming responsibility, she was a candidate from Kailali constituency no. 6 in the second Constituent Assembly as well. However, she was defeated. Subsequently, she became involved with the CPN (UML) and, becoming a central committee and politburo member of the CPN (UML), she also played the role of party in-charge for Kailali district. Along with the student movement, she has also presented herself as an activist by engaging in various aspects of social life. Naturally, she has played a more significant role in the women's movement. Especially to ensure one-third participation of women in various bodies of the state and in policy-making forums, whether by joining the party, or by joining the women's movement, or as an individual activist, she has played an important role. She can lead competently. In the course of fulfilling all these responsibilities, the role she played in the Constituent Assembly, the role she played as State Minister for Education, the roles she played in the women's movement and party politics, the ideas she put forward, the analyses and discussions she made, after studying these, the party believes that she can competently fulfill the responsibility as the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, and therefore, from the CPN (UML), from the parliamentary party, we have presented her as a candidate. After presenting this candidacy, we had hoped for support from the parliamentary parties of all parties. Naturally, we engaged in discussions and interactions, met with the honorable members of our parliamentary party, and with the honorable members of all parties. In the course of discussions and interactions, we must reach a consensus and send a message to the nation. Specifically, even if the first party or the second party had joined, when they joined, they would have taken all positions, such as the Deputy Speaker here. Similarly, the chairpersons of thematic committees would have been taken, considering the issue of majority-minority. Even if the first and second parties joined. Even if the second, third, and fourth parties joined. Even if the first and third parties joined. Such was the situation. But we did not want that. We want to continue the established values, norms, and practices of the National Assembly, and the message that the honorable members have been giving through the National Assembly. Whether in the context of law-making, or policy-making. Or in the context of making other decisions. We want to continue the consensus that has been established. We want to further consolidate our unity. We want to send a message to the nation that a national consensus has been reached here. Therefore, we have put her forward. After discussions and interactions with the honorable members of all parties, we reached a consensus, and I wish to inform you that her candidacy has been supported by all parties. We have made this decision by looking at the current situation and the future challenges of the National Assembly. The agreements we have made will gradually come before us through the agenda of the National Assembly. They will come tomorrow, they will come today, they will come tomorrow. We will take them forward sequentially. We have expressed that commitment. We have done these things to send a message to this nation. Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present to the assembly the proposal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now grant permission to Honorable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya to support the said proposal. Time: 5 minutes. Honorable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, I stand here to support Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari, the candidate for the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Lila Kumari Bhandari is a women leader who has contributed to Nepal's democratic movement for a long time. She has already contributed to this country by being a member of the Constituent Assembly and also as the State Minister for Education of the Government of Nepal, and she has gained that kind of experience. We believe that a person as experienced, honest, and capable as her can enhance the dignity of the National Assembly by being its Deputy Speaker, and for this reason, I stand here to support her. Honorable Chairperson, the National Assembly itself has a tradition of functioning through consensus. Even when there was a ruling party and an opposition party here, we have made every decision by consensus, and that is our past tradition. Therefore, to continue this, we believe that a personality like her can do it, and with this belief, Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I support the proposal presented to the assembly by Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now grant permission to Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary, another supporter of the said proposal, to support the proposal. Time: 5 minutes. Honorable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (JSP Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I support the proposal presented to the assembly by Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now grant permission to Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah (Garima), another supporter of the said proposal, to support the proposal. Time: 4 minutes. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, I am present at this rostrum to support the proposal presented by Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal that Honorable Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected to the post of Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly.

Since there was only one candidate, we have all come to know that he/she is a consensus candidate. He/she has come this far with long party experience. He/she has a long organizational background. He/she has successfully completed his/her role as a State Minister in the Constituent Assembly. In that sense, I stand today not personally, but on institutional and political grounds to support him/her. Today, we are not going to elect a person, but we are going to send a message of unity and cooperation to strengthen the capacity, impartiality, democracy, and socialist values of the parliament. In this sense, I consider this as an important journey of pride. Honorable Chairperson, Lila Kumari is about to be elected unanimously. Under her leadership, I would like to request that while doing so, today it is heard that Bhandari ji has also been involved in power-sharing. I would like to request that this is not about compromise, cooperation, or power-sharing. It is not just about political strategy. It is also the responsibility to save the republic, save the constitution, and strengthen democracy, and we have done this work by realizing and feeling that responsibility. Therefore, I stand here. The country has to be moved forward on the journey of socialism. The constitution must be protected and enriched. People's trust in the system must be established. In the future, this consensus will play an important role in making long-term policies and strategies in areas such as education, health, and employment. I would like to state this here. This is a matter of nation-building rather than power-sharing. I request that this be accepted in this way. It is also the tradition of our National Assembly to move forward through cooperation and coordination, and we have brought the republic through cooperation so far. The success of the Constituent Assembly was also due to cooperation, and in the coming days, we will have to take the path of cooperation for nation-building. The parliament should become a forum for dialogue, coordination, consensus, and cooperation. I wish the honorable member who is about to be elected success in fulfilling that responsibility. I also expect that he/she will take initiative to increase the dignity and calculation of the National Assembly, remain committed to the constitution, republic, and rule of law, and fully implement the rules of the National Assembly letter by letter. I also have confidence that he/she will perform his/her responsibilities independently and impartially while being elected to this post. In the future, political stalemates may also arise. The need to seek consensus by discussing with party leaders to end those political stalemates may also arise. We should accept and accept that in a natural and practical way. However, sometimes, by adhering to party directives, the dignity of this parliament is somewhat diminished. I would also like to remind you of this. Thirdly, I would like to state that he/she will play the role of an impartial referee in the implementation of the National Assembly rules, and with the permission of the Honorable Chairperson, I second the proposal put forth by Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal that Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari be elected as the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, as there is only one notice of proposal to elect Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari as the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly, as per Rule 8 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, Honorable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari has been declared elected unopposed as the Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly. Honorable members, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful tenure to the Honorable Lila Kumari Bhandari on her unopposed election to the esteemed position of Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister, to present the annual report of the Adivasi Janajati Aayog for the fiscal year 2081/082. Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: - (14:01 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the annual report of the Adivasi Janajati Aayog for the fiscal year 2081/082 to this honorable assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, a condolence motion is now presented on the demise of Ram Chandra Bhattarai, former member of the National Assembly. The National Assembly expresses deep sorrow on the demise of former member of the National Assembly, Ram Chandra Bhattarai, who was born on Ashoj 9, 1998 BS, at the age of 84 on Magh 13, 2082 BS. The late Bhattarai was a member of the National Assembly in 2056 BS from the Communist Party of Nepal (UML). This meeting expresses heartfelt tribute to the late Bhattarai and deep condolences to the bereaved family. I request the honorable members to pass the above condolence motion. Honorable members, I declare that the above condolence motion has been passed unanimously. Honorable members, let us now observe one minute of silence in mourning of the demise of former member of the National Assembly, Ram Chandra Bhattarai. (Silence) Thank you. Honorable members, this meeting is adjourned here, with the next meeting of the National Assembly to be held on Wednesday, Chaitra 25, 2082 BS, at 1:15 PM. (Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned here, to be held on Wednesday, Chaitra 25, 2082 BS, at 1:15 PM). Adjourned: 14:04 hrs.

sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasizes the need for legislative initiatives to empower local governments and calls for the National Assembly to play a crucial role in combating corruption and promoting good governance. They also highlight the importance of citizen participation and transparency in government processes.

speakers.topic: Role of National Assembly, good governance, citizen participation

sections.name: Tributes and Introductions
sections.summary_en: Honorable Dharmendra Paswan offers tributes to martyrs and expresses gratitude to policymakers and his political guru. He shares an anecdote about his guru's principle of inclusivity and thanks his party and supporters for his election.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan
speakers.topic: Tributes, gratitude, inclusivity principle

sections.name: Government Apology and Representation
sections.summary_en: Honorable Paswan acknowledges the government's apology to the Dalit community but cautions against repeating past mistakes. He commends the appointment of a minister from the Vadi community but expresses concern over the lack of Madhesi representation in the federal parliament.

speakers.topic: Dalit apology, representation, Madhesi issues

sections.name: Legislative Process and National Unity
sections.summary_en: Honorable Prem Prasad Dangal pays tribute to martyrs and congratulates newly elected members. He outlines three stages of legislation (pre-legislative, legislative, and post-legislative) and emphasizes the need for greater participation in the initial stage. He also stresses the importance of unity in diversity and ending all forms of discrimination.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dangal
speakers.topic: Legislative process, national unity, ending discrimination

sections.name: Call for Justice
sections.summary_en: Honorable Dangal calls for the immediate release of former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, describing his arrest as unjust and politically motivated.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dangal
speakers.topic: Release of KP Sharma Oli

sections.name: Commitment to Democracy and Development
sections.summary_en: Honorable Meena Singh Rakhal thanks her constituents and pledges to uphold democracy, fight corruption, and work for the nation's prosperity. She highlights the backwardness of Karnali Province and calls for special priority and policies to address its development challenges.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Meena Singh Rakhal
speakers.topic: Commitment to democracy, fighting corruption, Karnali development

sections.name: Attack on Democracy
sections.summary_en: Honorable Rakhal raises concerns about the treatment of former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and a Nepali Congress leader, viewing it as an attack on democracy, the constitution, and the rule of law, with potential implications for all citizens.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Meena Singh Rakhal
speakers.topic: Attack on democracy, constitution, rule of law

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The first speaker expresses concern about political retaliation and calls for the immediate release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak, warning of public protest if demands are not met.

speakers.topic: Political retaliation, release of leaders, democratic principles

key_issues: Release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Ranjit Karna pays tribute to martyrs, expresses pride in speaking for the first time, congratulates the new government, acknowledges past weaknesses in governance and employment, and offers cooperation from the Nepali Congress on issues like corruption control and institutional strengthening. He emphasizes the party's focus on youth employment and innovation, and readiness to support economic development and private sector facilitation. He reiterates the Congress's commitment to a 'constructive opposition' and responsible partnership, while also vowing to resist anti-people decisions. He calls for national unity and cooperation.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Ranjit Karna
speakers.topic: Tribute to martyrs, congratulations to new govt, national unity, cooperation

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Ram Kumari Jhankri expresses pride in being in the National Assembly, pays tribute to martyrs, and raises unanswered questions about past revolutions and the current state of democracy. She questions the peacefulness of the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests and calls for an impartial investigation into the destruction of Singha Durbar, demanding accountability.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Ram Kumari Jhankri
speakers.topic: Martyrs' tribute, unanswered questions, past revolutions, Singha Durbar destruction

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Rekha Kumari Jha highlights the issue of violence against women in Madhesh Province, particularly domestic violence, and its causes. She also discusses the challenges faced by women regarding citizenship and marriage registration. She calls for skill training and employment opportunities for women and urges the government to expedite the Civil Service Act. She reiterates the demand for the release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak, warning against state actions that undermine democracy.

speakers.name: Honorable Ms. Rekha Kumari Jha
speakers.topic: Violence against women, domestic violence, citizenship, Civil Service Act, release of leaders

key_issues: Release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: Honorable Roshni Mechhe delivered her first address to the National Assembly, expressing gratitude for the opportunity and paying tribute to martyrs. She thanked her party, KP Sharma Oli, and the voters of Koshi Province. She also offered congratulations and best wishes to the newly formed government, pledging constructive support and continuous oversight.
