speakers.topic: First address, gratitude, tribute to martyrs, support for government

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Lalit Jang Shahi spoke, paying tribute to martyrs and thanking his party, Nepali Congress, and the voters of Karnali Province. He emphasized the need to strengthen the nation and democracy, protect the constitution, and move beyond personal interests to focus on good governance and development. Honorable Lila Kumari Bhandari also spoke, thanking the Chairperson and her party leaders, and paying tribute to martyrs. She congratulated the new government and urged attention to rising inflation and black marketing, as well as digital violence and crimes against women. She also called for the release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak, criticizing the government's perceived vindictive actions.

speakers.topic: Tribute to martyrs, national interest, constitution, good governance

speakers.topic: Tribute to martyrs, congratulations to government, inflation, digital violence, release of leaders

sections.summary_en: Honorable Basudev Ghimire began his address, expressing pride in speaking for the first time and paying tribute to martyrs and expressing respect for the injured and families of martyrs. He thanked the Nepali Congress for nominating him.

speakers.name: Basudev Ghimire
speakers.topic: First address, tribute to martyrs, thanks to party

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The speaker expresses gratitude to the elected members and officials, congratulates newly elected members of the National Assembly and House of Representatives, and wishes success to the new government. The speaker emphasizes the need for national unity, consensus, and cooperation, warning against arrogance and revenge, and highlights that the nation's strength lies in the people's sentiment.

speakers.name: Honorable Member
speakers.topic: Gratitude, congratulations, national unity, government's role

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota thanks the National Assembly, pays tribute to martyrs, congratulates the new government, and expresses gratitude to her family and constituents. She emphasizes the house's role in lawmaking and national guidance, wishing the government success in prioritizing long-term national interest. She raises concerns about domestic violence, sexual violence, social discrimination, and the misuse of social media, calling for legal reforms and government accountability. She also advocates for the development of Gorkha district by connecting its historical and tourist sites with national development and tourism, and urges the federal government to expedite key projects in the district. Finally, she requests the release of former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak.

speakers.name: Samjhana Devkota
speakers.topic: National Assembly's role, social issues, Gorkha development, legal reforms

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa expresses happiness to be in the National Assembly and thanks his party and constituents. He states the Nepali Congress is open to constitutional amendments but stresses the difficulty in its creation. He calls for honoring all martyrs equally and advocates for a responsible role of the National Assembly in lawmaking. He raises concerns about the delay in publishing the Karki Commission report and the National Human Rights Commission report, emphasizing the right to information. He also highlights the need for economic development and suggests using the petroleum pipeline for facilitation.

speakers.name: Sunil Bahadur Thapa
speakers.topic: Constitutional amendment, martyrs' honor, right to information, economic development

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel thanks the chairperson and expresses gratitude to his party, supporting parties, and constituents. He pays tribute to martyrs and elders. As a representative of the oppressed Dalit community, he pledges to voice their concerns. He acknowledges the formation of a two-thirds majority government after a significant public mandate.

speakers.name: Somnath Poudel
speakers.topic: Gratitude, tribute to martyrs, Dalit representation, government mandate

The member also criticized a circular from the Prime Minister's Office that allegedly curtailed the rights of local and provincial governments, urging a return to the rule of law and constitutional supremacy. The member concluded by reaffirming commitment to the constitution, rule of law, and people's rights.
